Copy link
GitHub Copilot users can now connect to the Figma MCP server to push rendered UI to the Figma canvas as editable frames. You can also pull design context from Figma into code. Available today in VS Code and coming soon in the Copilot CLI.
This helps you:
Scope out new features or missing states in code, then push them to the canvas as a starting point for designers
Explore and compare directions together on the canvas before committing changes to code
Pull design context into Copilot to generate code that matches existing designs
Learn how to install the Figma MCP server.

Slots unlock dynamic components instances — from adding another menu option, button, or even an icon to your instances, without detaching.
Slots are great for:
Components with repeating elements, like task lists or tabs.
Components that are frequently customized, like cards or modals.
Simplifying bloated design systems by decreasing variants or hidden layers.
Reducing detaches so instances continue receiving updates from the main component.

Align all your code components with your Figma components in the Code Connect UI. Users now have the ability to:
Attach multiple code files to a single Figma component
See code previews across multiple frameworks (requires GitHub connection)
Set MCP instructions specific for each code framework to help agents implement those components correctly
This feature is now available for all Organization and Enterprise plans.
Learn more about getting started with the Code Connect UI in our developer documentation

Template picker updates in Figma Buzz
Update
Figma Buzz
Assets
Copy link
We’ve improved the template picker in Figma Buzz to make discovering and using templates simpler. Along with a visual refresh, all brand templates are now centralized under the “From [your company]” tab in a single view and organized by most recently published, rather than grouped by team. You can also now select and add multiple templates to the canvas at once directly from the template picker. These updates are rolling out this week.
Learn more about finding templates in Figma Buzz.

Starting today, you can generate Figma Design files from Codex using the Figma MCP server. The MCP server is built to support movement in both directions—bringing working UI onto the canvas and back into code just as easily—so you can build on your best ideas, not just your first.
This helps you:
Explore multiple approaches without rewriting code
Compare flows and states in one place
Share work for feedback without requiring a local setup
Move from implementation to exploration — and back again
You can learn more about using this feature and other Figma MCP server capabilities in our developer docs

In our latest Release Notes livestream, we covered the latest updates across our products, a live Q&A with Figma’s Chief Product Officer, and more—including a new way to work in Figma. Move from concept to completion using AI image tools, Make, and interactive prototypes.
Plus, we covered some new feature announcements:
Easier color variable binding
— Quickly find variables and styles directly in the color field, with smarter results as you type.
Learn more here.
Draw features available for plugin developers
— Access Figma Draw features like text on a path, dynamic strokes, and more to make plugins even more powerful.
Learn more here.

FigJam is now available in Notion as a pre-configured MCP integration:
Connect FigJam to Notion to automatically document meeting discussions and action items, and keep everything organized alongside your broader product work.
Generate FigJam diagrams directly from your Notion docs to map user journeys, create flow charts, and visualize ideas in seconds.
Read more about the MCP integration in our Help Center.

You can now share files, projects, and teams with an entire workspace. When you choose
Anyone in the workspace
, all members of that workspace get access, without making the content available to the rest of your org.
What’s new:
Share files, projects, and teams with
Anyone in the workspace
Everyone in the workspace gets access automatically, and only that workspace.
Content shared at the workspace level is discoverable in search for workspace members.
Learn more about Workspace-level sharing in our Help Center.
